theme: Air out of the AI trade & Ackman's quality bets · AI 거품 논쟁과 애크먼의 우량주 투자

tracks.title: Bill Ackman: AI's 'shiny object', Anthropic & his worst position (13 min)
tracks.show: Yahoo Finance · Interview with Brian Sozzi (Nov 13, 2026)

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I feel like markets are heading back to a little more sanity in a way.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: There's more focus on cash flows and business quality, and less what stocks can go the most in the next week.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So I would say a little bit more of a slightly longer-term orientation, I would say.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: When you say sanity, is that more reserved to the broader S&P 500 or some things we're seeing in tech?

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: I look at Neoclouds, I look at some of these AI momentum trades, a lot of them have been cut in half.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And I think that's the same.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I guess what I'm saying, you see, our bias is to own sort of these dominant long-term compounder businesses that we think have a very low probability of disruption in a highly disruptable world or disrupting world because of AI.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And I think a lot of the market's attention has been sort of on the shiny object.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And I think Neoclabs have been a bit of a shiny object.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: The AI trade generally, the picks and shovels of AI.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And the stuff that's been discarded are sort of the, what I would think of as the higher quality dominant companies that we'd like to own.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So it's been, we've made like seven new investments in the last six months and that a lot for us.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: It means that a bunch of companies got really cheap we've wanted to own for years.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: On the Sanity front bill, what, you know, I'm thinking I'm looking through, you know, the tech rubble that has been created over the over the last few weeks.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: Are you, does Sanity equate to you're a buyer here or looked at another way the Nasdaq is done falling?

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Yeah, I'm not going to give you a short term prediction.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I wouldn't, you know, I'm about 50% chance of being right, I would say, and 50% chance of being wrong.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Look, Look, I don't think stock market overall is expensive.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: To my point, I think there are a lot of stocks that have been obliterated or at attractive valuations.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And also, the overall earnings growth in the market has been very high.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And so the overall multiples with markets within range of where it's been historically, but I would say the quality of the businesses, the pace of growth, these longer term secular trends.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I'm a big believer that computes sort of an asset that you want to own over time.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I don't think you want to own it in a highly levered format, but I think AI is going to be a transformative technology.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I think it's going to drive growth.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I think it's going to help improve margins of good businesses.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: That's kind of the key factor.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: It's got to be a high quality business that is defensible.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: You and I have talked in the past about how you follow the work of Warren Buffet, and I know you're always focused on valuations and finding good value in the market.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: When you look at the likes of an entropic about to go public, is that business attractive to you?

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: Can you justify the valuation that they may get in public markets?

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I personally haven't done the work.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: A couple of guys on my team have done the work on entropic and actually came away positively inclined that there's a real business there, that they've got strong balance sheet, a but anytime you have a business that requires a massive investment in order to continue to accelerate its growth,

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: if you're wrong on how quickly the revenues are going to accelerate or how much capital is going to be required to meet the demand for the product or service you offer, it's a higher risk proposition.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: We think of ourselves as very low risk investors.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: You want to invest in businesses that we can predict with a very high degree of confidence.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And it's, I think, one topic is perhaps the most amazing business story of this century in terms of, you know, from zero to where it is today is an absolutely remarkable story.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Incredibly impressive story.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I think it's just a much more complicated question as to what that business is worth.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: It's very hard to nail that with any degree of precision.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: It could be worth a lot more, a lot less, depending upon a few variables that are difficult to predict.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And that's why it doesn't fit into our portfolio.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: How would you even go about you know, I come from the school of thought are you you know crunching working on discounted free cash flow models and Valuations and multiples.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: I mean, how do you even go about valuing a business?

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: That is that is losing billions might have to raise more money in his free cash flow negative

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Well, actually I think a dropping is on the cusp or might even be at a place In terms of its operating profitability where it's you know real operating profitability and that their investments I think they can make the argument.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Their investments in compute are about, well, I think the issue is if anthropic doesn't stay in the lead position, then the real question is about the business model.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So the capex they have to spend is really real.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I think it's just, it's also a cashflow model.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: It's just a much more complicated one to build than a widget company that sells 5% more widgets next year than the year before.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So I would just say a much more complicated question.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And there's a much wider range of outcomes.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And, you know, But it's a more speculative bet than buying, for example, Visa, a company we own.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: Well, that's what I wanted to ask you, because what's the most attractive or attractive stocks in your portfolio right now?

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So in terms of risk reward, my favorite position is two stocks.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: It's Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: These are stocks that have been completely discarded this year.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: The history goes back a while.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: But in fact, we've owned these stocks for 13 years.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: on the bet that they would eventually be released from conservatorship and be privatized again.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: That process began during Trump's original first term with Steve Mnuchin stopping the sweep of cash flows from the two companies, but Mnuchin ran out of time.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: The president in 2021 wrote a letter to Rand Paul saying, hey, this theft of Obama should never have happened.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: This thing called a network sweep.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And he sort of committed to, you know, if he were president, this never would have happened.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Well, he became president again.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And the stocks went from two or three dollars a share beginning right when he was elected to peaking at $70 a share last year, one of the better performers in the market.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And then the president tweeted a series of memes about taking them public, ringing the bell at the New York Stock Exchange.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And And the companies have done extremely well, rebuilt their capital, and in our view are ready to be released from conservatorship.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And the president was suggesting it could happen.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And even Howard Ludnick in September last year said, look, it could happen before the end of the year.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Well, the end of the year was 11 months ago.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: President's really done nothing, said nothing about them this calendar year.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And so those stocks have retraced.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: they're down 60 plus percent in this calendar year.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So they're our worst performing position that cost us probably 800, 900 basis points of performance.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: But the facts remain.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: What's interesting now with the midterms, the blue wave, so to speak, really handcuffs the president in terms of the things he can do in terms of economic policy, with one really big exception, which is Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And if the president falls through on what he said he would do, which he has a pretty good track record of doing, you know, these are, we think, $40, $50 stocks.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And today they're $4 stocks.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: You know, so this is a 10X that can happen with a tweet from the president, an opportunity for him to ring the bell, an opportunity for him to create a half a trillion dollar of the value of the American people, which 20% would go to the shareholders of which were won.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: But there are millions of small shareholders who own these stocks.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So that's the most, and I'm trading at a level where basically the market's saying the probability of this happening is very close to zero, and we think the probability of happening being actually quite high and in fact have the opportunity to meet and speak to the president about these companies.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And the treasury secretary recently, two weeks ago said, look, we're going to deal with it in the back half of the president's term, but not before midterms.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: That's the most interesting risk reward in the portfolio today.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: Do you still like Netflix and Microsoft?

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Yes, Microsoft's down the last couple days on a claw release, but we think they're in market position.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: The entry point, even for AI, for 450 million business seats, where companies like us, like the Microsoft 365, beyond the package of, You know, there are free versions of Excel and Word, Google and others have them, but what you want as an enterprise is,

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: you know, control cybersecurity protections.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: You want to be able to monitor what your teams are doing and you want to control their use, of course, of AI so that you don't burn, you know, fortune doing so.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And that platform that Microsoft has built over time is we think they're doing a very good job staying current in terms of enabling a new AI generation of workers.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And in fact, in Tropic, meaning I think it's something approaching 50% of their revenues coming through the hyperscaler, whether it's Amazon or Microsoft kind of being the gateway to access to AI and models for corporate users.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So we think Microsoft's position is really, really strong and people can come out with really good products that, you know, even if they're free, I don't think the major user, I think Microsoft position really remains a powerful one.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And we like it, you know, Netflix stocks down since we bought it, was down about 50%.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Since we bought it now, it's probably down 60% or so from the high, on kind of reduced, you know, as they call it, engagement, people spending, on average, less time with their Netflix subscription, that's a global statistic.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: You know, the different habits in different countries in terms of how people use Netflix.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: They also have been investing more in sports and other content differently from binge watching your favorite series.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: But in terms of subscription growth and renewals, they've remained strong.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: You know, they haven't had their next games, they made some changes in the C-suite in in terms of oversight of content creation and acquisition.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And you have to address maybe some received shortcomings.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: But that's a super cheap stock.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And this was a company trading on mid 30s or 30 plus time earnings today at 16, 17 times earnings.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And the business remains quite strong.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: What do you think the catalyst is for Netflix next year?

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: What has to happen to get that moving back up and to the right?

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: I think passage of time that just, you know, continued earnings growth, cash flow, revenues, some, you know, some additionally have some content wins.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And I think maybe better disclosure from the companies and people can have a better sense of how their subscriber base translates.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: You know, you made a really good point on, I think the, how entrenched we are with Microsoft's products.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: Are you, does that always surprise you to how quick the market reacts to when Enthropic comes out, they put out a demo of new software releases and the first thought is, wow, Enthropic is gonna put all software companies out of business or take 15% of Microsoft's business overnight.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Yeah, that was how we bought Microsoft in the first place.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: It was the so-called SaaS talk-a -blips.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And I think if you're a one product software company and you charge a high price and you're earning windfall profits, I think you're at risk.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: If you're the gateway to how people interact with the basic workflows of a desk worker, which is what Microsoft is today, I think it's a much more difficult position to dislodge.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: Think about the anthropics of the world do not have kind of a distribution channel, a sales channel and the same connectivity to all of these copies around the world in the way that Microsoft does.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: And that's a very valuable platform from which to sell additional products.

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: and it makes a lot of sense for a man to share a portion of the revenues for the opportunity to do business with approaching half a billion customers.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: Bill, you came out on X and you're staying on tech and defended video CEO Jensen Wong.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sozzi
transcript.text: Why did you feel compelled to come out and say something?

transcript.speaker: Bill Ackman
transcript.text: So one, I know him not well, but he's obviously been an unbelievable CEO and actually, on a very personal note, I reached out to him for some help with my daughter.

tracks.note: Ackman이 대부분 말해요(약 11분, 진행자 Brian Sozzi는 질문만). 0:00 시장이 '조금 더 제정신'으로 돌아온다 → 0:53 AI 'shiny object'와 버려진 우량주 → 2:44 Anthropic 상장, 왜 포트폴리오에 안 맞나 → 5:20 가장 좋아하는 종목 Fannie Mae·Freddie Mac(올해 최악 종목) → 8:17 Microsoft·Netflix → 12:36 Jensen Huang 이야기(13분에서 끊겨요). 스크립트는 자동 음성인식(whisper)이라 틀린 곳이 있어요: entropic / a dropping / one topic / in Tropic / Enthropic = Anthropic, Neoclabs = Neoclouds, network sweep = net worth sweep, Ludnick = Lutnick, falls through = follows through, claw release = Claude release, Jensen Wong = Jensen Huang. 1회차는 흐름만, 2회차는 스크립트를 보면서 들어요.

listening.task: 오늘은 Bill Ackman의 Yahoo Finance 인터뷰(2026년 11월 13일) 앞부분 13분이에요. 진행자 Brian Sozzi가 짧게 묻고 Ackman이 길게 답해요. 출근길(8:30–9:00)에는 0:00–5:20(시장의 'sanity', AI 'shiny object', Anthropic 이야기)을 1배속(어려우면 0.75배속)으로 흐름만 듣고, 퇴근길(17:30–18:10)에는 5:20–13:00(Fannie Mae·Freddie Mac, Microsoft, Netflix)을 들어요. 시간이 남으면 처음부터 한 번 더! 'a little more sanity', 'a bit of a shiny object', 'the picks and shovels of AI', 'very low risk investors'가 나오는 부분을 잘 들어 보세요. 바쁘면 Part 1의 처음 4분(~'that's why it doesn't fit into our portfolio')만 들어도 OK예요.

quiz.q: Why does Ackman say Anthropic doesn't fit into his portfolio? a) His team thinks it is not a real business, b) It is very hard to predict what it is worth — it needs massive investment and has a wide range of outcomes, c) He thinks AI will not change the economy
quiz.answer: b) Ackman 팀은 Anthropic이 '진짜 사업'이고 놀라운 성장 스토리라고 봤어요. 하지만 성장에 막대한 투자가 필요해서 가치를 정확히 예측하기 어렵고('very hard to nail that with any degree of precision'), 자신들은 'very low risk investors'라서 맞지 않는대요.

sentences.text: I feel like markets are heading back to a little more sanity in a way.
sentences.ko: 시장이 어떤 면에서는 조금 더 제정신으로 돌아가고 있는 것 같아요.

sentences.ko: 우리가 몇 년 동안 갖고 싶었던 회사들이 꽤 많이 아주 싸졌다는 뜻이에요.

sentences.text: It's got to be a high quality business that is defensible.
sentences.ko: 방어할 수 있는(해자가 있는) 고품질 기업이어야 해요.

sentences.text: We think of ourselves as very low risk investors.
sentences.ko: 우리는 스스로를 아주 위험이 낮은 투자자라고 생각해요.

sentences.text: I think it's just a much more complicated question as to what that business is worth.
sentences.ko: 그 회사가 얼마의 가치가 있는지는 훨씬 더 복잡한 문제일 뿐이에요.

reading.title: How much more air can come out of the AI trade?
reading.source: The Economist (public reprint via Hindustan Times)
reading.summaryKo: 11월 20일 나스닥이 하루에 5% 넘게 빠지며 10월 고점보다 20% 낮아졌고, 엔비디아는 한 달 만에 시가총액 2.7조 달러가 사라졌어요. 직접적인 계기는 불분명하지만, 깊은 이유는 분명해요: 시장이 드디어 'AI로 실제로 누가 돈을 버나?'를 묻기 시작했다는 것. Apollo의 Torsten Slok은 AI를 파는 기술기업의 현금흐름 전망(2028년까지 2배)과 AI를 사는 다른 산업의 전망이 서로 맞지 않는다고 지적했어요. 주가는 더 빠질 수 있지만(경기조정 PER은 닷컴 버블 수준), 'AI 도입 기업'의 이익률이 오르고 있다는 Morgan Stanley 자료도 있어요. 세 번째 시나리오: AI가 광고처럼 '안 쓰면 경쟁에서 지는' 필수 비용이 될 수도 있대요.
excerpt: TO THOSE WARNING of an artificial-intelligence bubble it sounded an awful lot like “pop”. On November 20th the NASDAQ index of technology stocks, home to AI’s biggest companies, deflated by over 5% in a day for the second time in just over a fortnight.
The deeper reasons behind the market softness, by contrast, are plain. Markets are at last grappling seriously with the question of who, if anyone, will make money from AI.
reading.tip: 'by contrast'로 '직접적 원인은 murky(불분명)하다 ↔ 깊은 이유는 plain(분명)하다'를 대비하는 구조를 보세요. 'who, if anyone, will make money'의 'if anyone'(그런 사람이 있기나 하다면)은 '아무도 못 벌 수도 있다'는 뉘앙스예요. 'grapple with'(씨름하다), 'portend'(예고하다), 'pots of money'(큰돈)도 Economist가 자주 써요.

vocab.example: A lot of the market's attention has been on the shiny object.

vocab.meaning: 곡괭이와 삽 — 붐의 '장비'를 파는 사업(예: AI 칩·데이터센터)

writing.prompt: Write 3–5 sentences in English: The Economist asks who, if anyone, will make money from AI. Who do you think will win — chipmakers, AI labs, or ordinary companies (like hospitals) that use AI? Why?
writing.question: Could AI help your clinical lab work better or cheaper? Give one example.
writing.hint: 이런 표현을 써 보세요: I think ... will make the most money because ... / In my lab, AI could help with ... / But the risk is ...

speaking.prompt: In one minute: Ackman likes 'dominant long-term compounder businesses' that AI cannot easily disrupt. Name one company you would hold for ten years and explain why.
phrases: I would hold ... for ten years because ...
speaking.alt: 쉬운 버전: Say three short sentences (e.g. I like Costco. People buy food every day. AI cannot replace it.).

evening.note: 목요일이에요. 지난번 읽은 데서 이어서 10페이지. 주말이 가까우니 피곤하면 5페이지만, 아니면 Minimum day도 OK.
